## Purpose and boundary

One-time owner test-handheld alignment before its next upgrade. This is a hard prerequisite for transferring another update into that handheld's update folder or rebooting it into an upgrade. Building engineering firmware, synthetic public-ROCKNIX/clean adoption QA, #515, #508 and #507 may proceed independently. No experimental-owner migration feature is added to the product.

#517 completed read-only byte/structure/local-counterpart verification with explicit limits. #516 owns personal residue classification and the separate cloud cleanup proposal. This task owns the device pre-upgrade sequence and its verifiable release gate. Precise private inventories, selected paths, hashes and findings stay local.

## Maintainer requirement (verbatim)

> Is there a reason the local safe scope would be exactly one less than the cloud file count? I agree with the reusable verification protocol￼concept and think that will add value. Let’s make sure we have a task for any of the controlled alignment necessary and be sure that we do that before we attempt an upgrade. I want to make sure we deal with any leftover mutation files, et cetera, as well. In terms of next steps, if we have a solid understanding and well-defined tasks for how we get to our next release candidate, I’d like to begin that work.￼

## Work in order

1. Bind a new private plan to the actual installed firmware, current selected roots, configuration, automatic-sync settings and migration/recovery/scan state. Reconcile any owner cloud rename before choosing pointer values. Never infer settings rollback from a cloud rewind.
2. Trace each candidate residual artifact's current reader/writer. Distinguish obsolete migration/mutation records and stale scan/temp state from active metadata, real save versions, recovery copies and credentials. Produce an exact keep/archive/remove disposition with source evidence and a reversible host/device retention plan. Uncertain entries remain preserved.
3. Prove the exact pre-upgrade sequence with synthetic existing-state fixtures: prevent all relevant automatic transfer/migration consumers before pointer changes or retiring their records, align only agreed settings, handle obsolete state, and read back the result. Deleting a pending record can reactivate old code; do not require installing the replacement firmware first, since the owner requires alignment before the upgrade. If isolating old consumers is necessary, name that action and prove it in the sequence.
4. Present the concrete named device actions with files/settings written, retained evidence, rollback and network effects. Obtain any still-required per-action authorization under docs/device-testing-policy.md, then execute through tools/device-act. This tracking request does not authorize arbitrary deletion, credential export, cloud movement, a sync, or an upgrade now.
5. Retain a private acceptance receipt bound to current device/configuration state and its intended next image; add a redacted gate result here and in the deployment handoff. Any relevant intervening state change invalidates the acceptance and requires recheck. Transfer/reboot still require their own named scope.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A source-cited private state/residue manifest and concrete per-key/per-path plan distinguishes keep/archive/remove and preserves personal saves, credentials, active metadata and recovery copies. #516's relevant classification is incorporated; unknown residue is not silently deleted.
- [ ] A synthetic rehearsal proves the pre-upgrade order, automatic-consumer isolation, no unintended transfer/migration reactivation, interruption/failure behavior, rollback and unchanged save payload hashes. Commands and terminal receipts identify what was actually exercised.
- [ ] Named authorized device actions complete before the next update transfer/reboot. Exact readback proves aligned selected roots and intended auto-sync state, obsolete records handled as planned, no unintended writer active and preserved payload/recovery hashes. No claim of completion rests on intent alone.
- [ ] A sealed private acceptance receipt and redacted tracker/handoff status block upgrade until completion and invalidate on relevant state drift. Subsequent upgrade and first deliberate sync retain separate action authority and post-upgrade readback.

Can this be done on the VM? Yes for the proposed sequence and old/new consumer behavior with synthetic state. Actual private-state alignment is a separately authorized operational action, not a release QA fixture. It is a prerequisite for this particular handheld's next upgrade, not for host builds or common VM qualification. Use active job/result supervision if a step is long; preserve compact evidence and retire disposable fixtures after proof.


## Source-derived preparation — 2026-10-08

The exact installed distribution/ES consumers are traced in a private operational proposal. The finite public-synthetic old-helper proof now qualifies13 distinct controls: unguarded join/follow can rewrite pointers while the transfer lock is held; the exact historical-path keep guard suppresses those automatic changes; five transfer/apply entrypoints refuse under the lease. Some old content paths still perform discovery before refusal, so the lease is not network isolation. Protected synthetic payload, recovery and credential hashes stayed equal. Root verified285 sealed evidence files; initial overstrict read-oracle failures remain retained separately.

Proposed alignment order: classify live recovery/startup-hook state; quiesce old consumers; preserve exact originals; update automatic-sync guards and both live/fallback configurations; archive only identified stale migration/scan records; verify unchanged saves/recovery; restore original frontend service state under qualified guards. Unknown records remain preserved. No blanket cache deletion, cloud move, personal payload rewrite or unattended frontend mask across upgrade.

The helper proof is not transaction/systemd/restart proof or device acceptance. Remaining work is bounded live readback, exact reversible execution/failure/restart rehearsal, named device actions and a state-bound receipt tied to the intended next image. Any relevant drift invalidates it. This task stays open and remains a prerequisite before the owner's next update transfer/reboot. No device or personal-cloud action occurred during this preparation.
